That is exactly the reuse-vs-new analysis the rubric demands: the doc would add a second, independently pinnable `Now func() int64` inside the same daemon, so finish-route tests and coordinator behavior can be pinned to different notions of 'now' in the same process with no error. result.proposed_fix: Replace the precedent bullets in section 2 with an explicit reuse analysis, e.g.: 'The daemon already injects a clock seam: coordinator.Config.Now func() int64, wired to the wall clock at daemon.go:836. Add verification row V14: `grep -rn '&Daemon{' --include='*.go' .` (all packages, non-test included) proving every construction site goes through New, or asserting per-site why a literal cannot reach the finish route; and either run the deferred full `go test ./...` locally before handoff or state explicitly that AC-4 makes CI the first full-suite check. result.strongest_objection: In T3 (`TestEpisodeFinishRecordRechecksScopeExpiry`), mutating `d.now` across sequential HTTP requests to `d` could trigger a data race under `-race` if `d` runs background goroutines that also read `d.now`, or if an HTTP handler overlaps with the test's write to `d.now`. Currently `d.now` is only read in `episode_finish.go` synchronously during the request and `pinFinishClock` is called between synchronous requests, which explains why `-race -count=200` (V10) passed, but if future callers read `d.now` from background loops without synchronization, mutating the function pointer directly on `Daemon` in tests will race.
